Musa is a messenger whom Allah the Exalted sent to Pharaoh and his people, and supported with two miracles: one of them is the staff that swallowed the serpents; the other was his hand, which he would put into his bosom and it would come out white without any blemish. Musa called to the oneness of Allah, so Pharaoh fought him and gathered the sorcerers against him to plot against him, but he defeated them by the permission of Allah the Exalted. Then Allah commanded him to leave Egypt with those who followed him, and Pharaoh pursued him with a great army; and when his followers thought they would be overtaken, Allah commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, so that it would be his salvation and the destruction of Pharaoh, whom Allah made a lesson for others.

But the trial of Samiri occurred, leading the Israelites to worship a golden calf that lowed. Aaron called them back to worship Allah instead of the calf, but they grew arrogant. When Moses returned and saw what his people had come to, he reproached Aaron severely.

He is the Friend of Allah; Allah chose him for His message and favoured him over many of His creation. Ibrahim lived among a people who worshipped the stars, and that did not satisfy him; he sensed by his innate nature that there is a greater God, until Allah guided him and chose him for His message. Ibrahim began calling his people to the oneness of Allah and His worship, but they denied him and tried to burn him, and Allah saved him from their hands. Allah made the prophets from the progeny of Ibrahim: Isma‘il and Ishaq were born to him. Ibrahim built the Ka‘bah together with Isma‘il.

She endured and worked to provide their daily food until Allah healed him and replaced everything in which he was tested. Thus Ayyub is cited as an example of patience and affliction. It is related that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will use Ayyub, peace be upon him, as an argument against those afflicted.

Ishmael: Abraham's firstborn and the son of Lady Hagar. At Allah's command Abraham took Hagar and her son to the site of Mecca, leaving them with a little water and dates. When provisions ran out, she walked back and forth until Allah guided her to Zamzam water. Many people came to her. Then Allah commanded our master Abraham to build the Kaaba and raise the House's foundations: Ishmael brought stones while Abraham built until they completed it. Then came Allah's command to sacrifice Ishmael: Abraham saw in a dream that he slaughtered his son and told him. He replied, 'Father, do what you are commanded; Allah willing, you will find me patient.' Allah ransomed him with a great sacrifice. Ishmael was a horseman, the first to tame horses, patient and forbearing. He is said to be the first to speak clear Arabic. He kept his promises, commanded his family to pray and give zakat, and called for worshipping Allah and His oneness.

Idris was a truthful prophet and one of the patient, the first prophet sent on earth after Adam and the father of Noah's grandfather. Thirty scrolls were revealed to him. He called to Allah's oneness, and a thousand people believed in him. He was the first to write with a pen, sew and wear sewn clothes, and study the stars and their courses.

Dhun-Nun: nun means the great fish; Dhun-Nun is the prophet Jonah, peace be upon him, named so because the fish swallowed him and then released him from its belly. Allah sent Jonah to Nineveh. He called them to worship Allah alone, but they refused arrogantly. He left, threatening punishment after three nights. They feared for themselves, believed, and Allah lifted the punishment. Jonah sailed on a ship. When they were about to sink, they cast lots to choose a man to throw overboard; three times the lot fell on Jonah. He threw himself into the sea and the fish swallowed him. Allah inspired it not to eat him. Jonah prayed to his Lord to bring him out of the darkness. Allah answered and sent him to a hundred thousand people or more.
